legend: With a rush of people buying gifts for Valentine's Day, Magikarp is waiting in a line of n$$$n$$$ people at KarpMart when he notices that out of the n$$$n$$$ people in line, there are exactly k$$$k$$$ subarrays of length 4 where the people are lined up in increasing height order. Magikarp now wonders: if these n$$$n$$$ people were to rearrange themselves, how many total permutations would also have exactly k$$$k$$$ length-4 subarrays with increasing height order. Print your answer in mod 109+7$$$10^9+7$$$.
Assume that all n$$$n$$$ people have different heights.
input: The first line of input contains 2 integers n$$$n$$$ and k$$$k$$$ (4≤n≤500,0≤k≤n−3)$$$(4\le n\le 500, 0\le k\le n-3)$$$ — the number of people and the number of desired increasing length-4 subarrays.
output: Output a single integer in mod 109+7$$$10^9+7$$$, the total number of permutations with exactly k$$$k$$$ length-4 subarrays of increasing heights.
